claims.explanation: Hydroxyfasudil is a ROCK inhibitor whose known biology centers on activating PI3K/Akt-eNOS signaling and modulating actin cytoskeleton/mechanical signaling. Selective killing may therefore depend on PTEN/PI3K-Akt pathway status and on Rho/ROCK-dependent cytoskeletal or survival signaling, with PTEN loss or PI3K pathway activation sensitizing cells and intact PTEN/Akt signaling protecting them.

features.basis: PTEN-mutant lines are enriched among selectively killed lines, consistent with PI3K/Akt dependence and ROCK-inhibitor modulation of Akt signaling
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear among killed lines, suggesting PI3K/Akt pathway activation increases sensitivity
Most selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations, though this is common across cancer lines and may reflect broader genomic instability
ARID1A mutations recur in killed lines, possibly linking chromatin remodeling/cytoskeletal stress responses to ROCK inhibition
ATM mutations appear in several killed lines, suggesting DNA-damage/checkpoint defects may enhance sensitivity
BRCA2 mutations are present in multiple killed lines, possibly reflecting homologous-recombination deficiency
NF1 mutations occur in killed lines and may activate RAS/PI3K signaling
STK11 mutations appear in killed lines, potentially altering AMPK/mTOR and survival signaling
BRAF-mutant lines are more frequent among least-affected lines, suggesting MAPK-driven survival may reduce sensitivity
KRAS-mutant lines appear among least-affected lines, suggesting RAS/MAPK activation may protect from ROCK inhibition
Higher ROCK1 expression would increase dependence on ROCK signaling and sensitivity to hydroxyfasudil
eNOS expression is increased by hydroxyfasudil and mediates protective Akt/NO signaling, so high baseline eNOS may reduce killing
